To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intake of a sheep cheese naturally enriched in ALAs, CLAs and VAs improves the lipid profile of hypercholesterolametic subjects and more remarkably reduces the levels of anandamides in the blood.

consumption of an enriched cheese, containing a high amount of CLA, ALA and VA, significantly reduces the plasma anandamide levels in hypercholesterolemic subjects, with a concomitant decrease in LDL-cholesterolemia.
a sheep cheese, enriched in n-3 fatty acid, CLA and vaccenic acid, improves plasma lipid profile and reduces the anandamide content in mildly hypercholeseterolaemic subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the intake of dairy fat enriched in CLA, VA and ALA, which may have beneficial effects in hypercholesterolemic subjects.
the potential of sheep cheese as a functional food, and suggests the possibility of using it in the prevention of CVD.
the possibility that the intake of a naturally enriched cheese may be a dietary strategy to reduce the risk of CVD in hypercholesterolemic subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intake of enriched dairy fat, in the context of an overall healthy diet, may represent a valid strategy in preventing and/or controlling hypercholesterolemia and CVD, and may also be useful in reducing body weight.
the present results support the view that the dairy fat from sheep is a healthy food for the human being.
the intake of enriched cheese is safe and beneficial for hypercholesterolemic subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sheep cheese naturally enriched in ALAs, CLAs and VAs is an excellent food for the prevention of CVD, and that it may be considered as a functional food.
a sheep cheese, rich in ALA, VA and CLA, improves the plasma lipid profile and reduces endocannabinoids in the plasma of mildly hypercholesterolameric subjects.

the sheep cheese, naturally fortified in ALA, VA and CLA, is able to improve lipid profile, reduce anandamide and increase the n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs) in mildly hypercholes-terolaemic subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the intake of a sheep cheese enriched with ALA, CLAs and VA, in addition to the beneficial effects on lipid metabolism, may also be effective in reducing the endocannabinoids in hypercholesterolemia, which is a risk factor for the development of metabolic disorders and CVD.
the intake of dairy products, especially those with a high content of n-3 fatty acid, is a promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of hypercholesterolamia.

the use of pasture and lipid supplementation to enrich sheep cheese in n-3 fatty acid, CLA and vaccenic acid, is a promising strategy to reduce the risk of CVD in mildly hyperchoesterolaemic subjects.
